visual_goal: Show authority over the Lisbon booking passing between systems like a relay baton, with a reconciliation proving each transfer underneath.
prompt: A left-to-right relay illustration. Along the top runs a chain of five boxes joined by solid thick arrows, each arrow carrying a small relay baton: at the far left 'Booking platform', next 'Northmere Pay', next 'Subledger', next an open book labeled 'Ledger', and at the far right a stacked-layers box labeled 'Consolidation'. Above 'Northmere Pay', a plain generic office building labeled 'Provider' with one solid arrow down into 'Northmere Pay'; below-left of 'Northmere Pay', a bank building labeled 'Bank' with one solid arrow into 'Northmere Pay'. Along the bottom of the canvas runs a wide orange band with a balance-scale icon labeled 'Reconciliations'. Three thin dotted arrows drop straight down into the band: one from 'Northmere Pay', one from 'Subledger', one from 'Ledger'.
alt: Authority passes like a relay baton from the booking platform to Northmere Pay, the subledger, the ledger and consolidation, with provider and bank feeding Northmere Pay and dotted lines from each hand-off down to reconciliations that prove the transfer.

visual_goal: Show authority enforced in three stacked layers, preventive, contractual and detective, with the detective layer feeding the data owner and design authority who update the matrix.
prompt: A top-to-bottom layered illustration of three wide horizontal bands stacked like a filter. The top band, blue, with a padlock on a pen icon, labeled 'Preventive'. The middle band, teal, with a signed contract icon, labeled 'Contracts'. The bottom band, orange, with a magnifying glass icon, labeled 'Detective'. A few small grey dots fall from above: most stop on the top band, a few on the middle band, and the last ones are caught by the magnifying glass in the bottom band. One arrow from the bottom band goes right, labeled 'breaks', into a desk with a gavel labeled 'Data owner' and a desk with a blueprint labeled 'Design authority', side by side. From those desks one arrow goes up to a small grid document labeled 'matrix'.
alt: Three stacked enforcement layers, preventive write-path controls, boundary contracts and detective checks, with breaks from the detective layer going to the data owner and design authority, who update the authority matrix.

visual_goal: Show the authority for merchant commission invoices moving from SFP to FI-CA through a parallel run and cohort cutovers, with each partner having exactly one issuing system at any moment and rollback possible per cohort.
prompt: A left-to-right migration roadmap illustration with exactly three gold crowns in the whole picture. At the far left, a blue box labeled 'SFP' wearing a gold crown. Next, under one bracket labeled 'Parallel run' and the date 'April 2028', a blue box 'SFP' wearing a gold crown beside a plain green box 'FI-CA' with a bare head and a calculator icon, and a balance scale between them. Next, a bridge under the label 'cohort cutover' and the date 'May 2028': small groups of houses cross the bridge one group at a time, and each house is joined by a single thin line to exactly one box. Next, a green box labeled 'FI-CA' wearing a gold crown, with the date '31 Dec 2028' below it. At the far right, a greyed-out box labeled 'SFP read-only' holding an archive drawer. Four forward arrows join these elements left to right. Below the bridge, one orange dashed curved arrow starts at the middle of the bridge and curves back left underneath, ending under the balance scale of the parallel run; it is labeled 'rollback'. The final crowned 'FI-CA' box has only its forward arrows.
alt: A roadmap moving invoice authority from SFP through a parallel run in April 2028 and cohort cutovers from May 2028 to FI-CA by 31 December 2028, with SFP kept read-only for history and rollback possible per cohort.
